definitions.explanation: The Romance language originating in Spain, spoken as a native language in Spain, most of Latin America, and several other countries.

examples.japanese: スペイン{語|ご}を{勉強|べんきょう}している。
スペイン{語|ご}は{世界|せかい}で{二番目|にばんめ}に{母語話者|ぼごわしゃ}が{多|おお}い{言語|げんご}だ。
examples.english: Spanish is the language with the second-largest number of native speakers in the world.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}で{第二外国語|だいにがいこくご}としてスペイン{語|ご}を{選|えら}んだのは、{将来|しょうらい}{南米|なんべい}で{働|はたら}きたいと{思|おも}ったからだ。
examples.english: I chose Spanish as my second foreign language at university because I wanted to work in South America in the future.

notes:
Formed from スペイン (Spain) + {語|ご} (language). Spanish is one of the more popular foreign languages studied in Japan, especially at the university level as a {第二外国語|だいにがいこくご} (second foreign language). Japanese has borrowed some words from Spanish, particularly through early contact with Portuguese and Spanish missionaries in the 16th century.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スペイン{語|ご}を{話|はな}す: to speak Spanish
- スペイン{語|ご}の{授業|じゅぎょう}: Spanish class
- スペイン{語|ご}{圏|けん}: Spanish-speaking world
- スペイン{語|ご}{検定|けんてい}: Spanish language proficiency test

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ポルトガル{語|ご}: Portuguese — closely related Romance language
- フランス{語|ご}: French — another popular second foreign language choice in Japanese universities
- {英語|えいご}: English — the primary foreign language studied in Japan
